claim: Writing a Z80 DMA WR4 byte with 'interrupt control follows' ($91) locks the Next DMA until the machine is reset (power-off, or an F4 soft reset on core 3.03.00); do not port such code onto the zxnDMA.
limit: Only byte $91 tested, on the N-Go board (Issue 2-compatible clone, core 3.03.00) and a Kickstarter 3 board (core 3.03.03); DMA resets ($C3 x6, $A3, $AF, $8B) do not free it.

evidence.text: N-Go board (Issue 2-compatible clone), core 3.03.00: after WR4 byte 91 then 87 every later transfer failed; six C3 resets, A3, AF, 8B did not recover it, only power-off.

N-Go board (Issue 2-compatible clone), core 3.03.00 (nxsuite XH2): one byte copied before WR4 $91, none after it; after an F4 soft reset the DMA answered again. An earlier run of an older build: a power-cycle frees it too.
